newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gold Fields Namibia mine closed to mid-Feb.
newsitem.headline: Gold Fields Namibia mine closed to mid-Feb.

text.p: Gold Fields Namibia Ltd said on Monday that its Kombat mine will only reopen in mid-February after flooding shut down the operation only weeks after it reopened following a lengthy strike.
Gold Fields Namibia subsidiary Tsumeb Corp Ltd's Financial Manager Jan du Plessis said the mine would probably only reopen in the middle of next month.
"Six weeks is a more accurate assessment," du Plessis said by telephone from Namibia.

He said some 1,200 tonnes of copper would be lost in production due to the flooding which followed a breakthrough of fissure water on January 7 in a development drive some 300 metres below the surface.
Du Plessis said the mine would start pumping water from the flooded area on Tuesday.
He said Kombat would try and make up the losses in copper production through gains of 655 tonnes of lead and just over a tonne of silver.
Kombat is one of three mines operated by Tsumeb Corp Ltd which were hit by a crippling three-month strike affecting both the mines and smelter last year.

Tsumeb said at the time the strike was resolved that it planned to produce around 27,000-28,000 tonnes of blister copper in 1997 and 30,000 tonnes of lead. Production in 1995 was just under 30,000 tonnes of copper and 27,000 tonnes of lead.
Most of the company's lead is produced from bought-in material while copper output is from the three mines.
Gold Fields Namibia is part of the Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd group.
